transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-25
Time: 11:00 AM UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Gupta (Redwood AE), Evan Lee (Redwood SE), Sonia Patel (PearlBridge - Head of Platform), Marco Ruiz (CTO), Hannah Cole (DevOps)

Summary (auto): quick renewal check-in, discuss capacity uplift and EU/APAC region activation, VPC onboarding windows, SOC2/KMS questions, next steps and pilot sizing.

[00:00] Maya: ok good morning everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick agenda: renewal numbers, ask about traffic growth, preferred region additions, and any outstanding security/legal blockers.
[00:18] Sonia: yeah thanks Maya, um quick note we are on track to double inference calls by Q1, we hit a spike last month where p95 latency crept up and the ops team flagged it.
[00:33] Evan: got it. do you recall the profile? short chat sessions or long documents? that changes batching and kv cache benefits.
[00:42] Hannah: it's mixed, roughly 70% short chat (20-60 tokens) and 30% long form summarization (avg 800 tokens). the long ones are what crept the lat. also we want EU region for residency and lower egress for EU customers.
[00:59] Maya: perfect — thats helpful. for renewal we proposed a 12-month extension with a 20% capacity uplift and an optional EU burst add-on. wanted to check whether you'd prefer dedicated nodes (reserved) or to stay hosted and use routing/fallback?
[01:17] Marco: honestly leaning to dedicated in EU for predictable latency and compliance. but we are cost sensitive — dedicated committed GPUs are heavier capex. if Hosted with private VPC and stronger SLAs is possible, that could be attractive.
[01:36] Evan: quick nuance — dedicated capacity gives you pinned throughput and lower jitter; hosted with routing works but when peak happens you might see model variant fallbacks. we can set warm standby and regional failover but it is a tradeoff.
[01:51] Sonia: can you remind us about KMS and audit logs? our security team needs HSM-backed keys and full API-level audit trails.
[02:01] Maya: yes — Redwood Private (VPC) supports customer-managed KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML, RBAC and audit logs. small caveat: on-prem HSM requires a slightly different onboarding timeline. we'll share the whitepaper.
[02:15] Hannah: transcript is a little fuzzy — when you say KV cache, we often hear K-V cash in notes — just so we align: we rely heavily on prefix caching for short sessions.
[02:26] Evan: haha, noted. yes prefix KV cache — sorry for the slur. on batching: we can tune batching profiles to prioritize p99 SLO, keep latency SLOs while still getting cost savings.
[02:40] Marco: what's your p99 targets with dedicated EU nodes? we need sub-300ms for 95% of short chats and sub-800ms for long forms.
[02:51] Evan: with dedicated A100-class pools and tuned kernels, we typically see p95 ~120-180ms for small tokens, p99 can be ~260-320ms depending on sequence length distribution. long 800-token runs will be higher; we recommend asynchronous streaming for those. we can run a baseline benchmark.
[03:12] Sonia: ok, benchmark needed. also curious about quantization — you mentioned q4 and int8 somewhere in the docs, how stable is that for summary quality?
[03:23] Evan: Great question — quantization helps reduce cost and memory; we have model recommender that flags which model+quant combo has acceptable QA. for some models int8 changes some probabilities; we run evals on your prompt sets as part of Redwood Optimize to measure regressions.
[03:40] Maya: jumping back to contract — you currently have 6 months left, correct? renewal window is within 30 days of expiry. our proposed amendment adds EU region activation as a billed add-on and moves you to a 12-month committed tier with a modest discount.
[03:56] Marco: correct, contract expires mid-November. would prefer a 12-month extension if pricing is reasonable and we can lock in a dedicated EU pool in Q1.
[04:08] Maya: sounds reasonable. action: I'll send revised quote with regional line items.
[04:15] Hannah: one more ops detail — we need egress accounting, do you bill per token + egress separately? also data retention for logs?
[04:24] Maya: hosted charges are per-token + optional egress billing. for Dedicated/Private, some egress can be part of the contract depending on commitment; we'll call that out. logs retention and audit trails are configurable; longer retention is an add-on.
[04:36] Sonia: security review — do you have SOC2 type II? and do you support customer-managed keys in AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault?
[04:45] Evan: yes SOC2 Type II, ISO paperwork available. KMS integration supports AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault; for HSM we can integrate via a supported partner, will surface the architecture diagram.
[04:58] Marco: any gotchas for VPC peering? our infra team is tight on network ranges and we prefer dedicated private link.
[05:08] Evan: PrivateLink / VPC Peering supported. customer-managed routing and egress IPs can be set. provisioning lead time is typically 3-4 weeks for EU dedicated nodes + VPC if capacity is available; on-prem longer.
[05:22] Sonia: timeline is tight — we need EU active by mid-Jan. is that feasible?
[05:28] Maya: mid-Jan for EU dedicated nodes is feasible if we sign by early November and commit capacity; otherwise we can do hosted EU region sooner as a stop-gap.
[05:39] Hannah: pilot idea: start with hosted EU region + canary traffic, then switch to dedicated for production after contract is in place. can we do that?
[05:47] Evan: absolutely, we can do canary routing and pin certain routes to dedicated once provisioned. that’s exactly what our rollout tools support (canary/A-B and fallback).
[05:58] Marco: costs — curious about burst capacity. sometimes we have 2-3x spikes; do you charge differently for burst vs reserved?
[06:06] Maya: reserved committed capacity has a lower unit price and predictable monthly bill. burst is metered at a higher rate; we also offer a burst pool add-on with capped overage rates for enterprise customers. we can model scenarios with your traffic CSV.
[06:21] Evan: also worth mentioning smart batching and prefix caching reduce token costs during steady workloads — we can show a cost model with and without caching.
[06:29] Sonia: yes please. also legal needs to see the amendment language for data residency. can we get a redline?
[06:36] Maya: we'll prepare an amendment draft for PearlBridge to review; legal can loop in.
[06:41] Hannah: ops request — can you share runbooks for incident escalation? we want the on-call flow and typical RTO/RPO.
[06:49] Evan: we'll include runbook excerpts — basic SRE escalation, per-route health checks, and incident playbooks.
[06:55] Sonia: excellent. one oddball: we're trialing a text-to-structured output feature — tool-calling stuff — will Redwood support tool-calls and structured JSON outputs?
[07:05] Evan: yes Redwood supports streaming, structured outputs, and function/tool-calling via the API. small transcription note: sometimes the SDK names get mangled in notes, like Redwood console vs Redwood Console — but feature exists.
[07:18] Marco: ok wrapping — can you confirm the exact deliverables and dates?
[07:22] Maya: Sure: 1) revised quote and amendment draft (Maya, by 2026-10-28) 2) SOC2 / KMS docs and runbook excerpts (Evan, by 2026-10-27) 3) customer to share traffic profile & legal contacts (Hannah/Marco, by 2026-10-29) 4) schedule pilot sizing & benchmark (Evan/Maya, by 2026-11-02).
[07:46] Sonia: that works. any open questions from Redwood?
[07:50] Evan: just confirm preferred EU datacenter (we have eu-west-1 and eu-central-1) and whether you want Japan vs Singapore for APAC later.
[07:59] Marco: prefer eu-central-1 and Singapore for APAC.
[08:04] Maya: noted. one last thing — competitors were flagged by your infra team; we can do a short side-by-side on latency/cost vs Anthropic-like providers, but we'll keep it neutral.
[08:16] Sonia: yes please. we'll need that for the exec readout.
[08:21] Maya: Great. recap: we'll get docs & quote this week, schedule pilot next week, and follow up with legal redline. thanks everyone.

[08:30] (call closes — informal chatter about holiday planning)

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker labels blurred by auto-diarization; some product names appear with small typos (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache, "Redwood console" spelled differently). The body contains natural speech, interruptions, and filler words.
